finding.summary: No test that a guard is *un*registered when `active` flips true→false or the guarded component unmounts
finding.evidence: The only "not guarded" case renders with `active={false}` from the start (`navigation-guard.test.tsx:105-112`), so `register`'s returned cleanup in `use-navigation-guard.ts:52-55` is never exercised. Nothing asserts that after a document finishes saving (mayHaveUnsent → false) or after the editor unmounts, the stale guard stops being asked. If that cleanup regressed, a stale closure would keep returning a prompt and every subsequent in-app navigation, app-wide, would pop "Leave without saving?" forever — a visible break the green suite would not catch. Neither sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx nor navigation-guard.test.tsx toggles `active` after mount.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exercises guard unregistration on `active` true→false or on unmount. A direct counterexample exists in the very file cited: navigation-guard.test.tsx:186-211, `it('stops asking once the component that registered the guard is gone')`. It renders a `Toggling` harness with `<Editor active guard={blocking} />`, rerenders with the editor unmounted, then clicks the leaving link and asserts no PROMPT.title appears and 'workspace page' renders. That unmount runs the effect cleanup returned at use-navigation-guard.ts:56, which is the unregister closure created at navigation-guard-provider.tsx:95-97 (`guardsRef.current.delete(guard)`). If that cleanup regressed, the stale guard would remain in `guardsRef`, `push` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:118-135) would find it still returning PROMPT (guardRef still holds `blocking`), the dialog would open and both assertions would fail — precisely the 'prompts forever' regression the finding describes. The test is therefore meaningful, not vacuous. The `active` true→false flip runs the identical cleanup via the same `useEffect(..., [active, register])`. The reviewer's quoted evidence also mismatches the tree (the `active={false}` case is at 111-118, not 105-112, and is not the only non-guarded case), indicating a stale read.

finding.summary: The `pathOf`/`leaving` path comparison is only ever tested under `MemoryRouter` with no basename, while the app mounts the router with `VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME`
finding.evidence: `leaving()` compares `navigator.createHref(to)` against `navigator.createHref(locationRef.current)` (provider lines ~36 and ~100-106). Both tests render `<MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/s/doc-1']}>` with no `basename` (navigation-guard.test.tsx:58, sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx:~86), whereas App.tsx passes `basename={import.meta.env.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME}`. `useLocation()` returns a basename-stripped pathname while `createHref` re-applies the basename, so a basename deployment exercises a code path no test covers: if the two sides ever resolve differently the guard silently never fires (edits lost) or fires on every same-page query update. No test sets a basename anywhere for this component.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test ever exercises the pathOf/leaving comparison under a router basename. A dedicated test exists: navigation-guard.test.tsx:128-150, 'resolves the same-page exemption under a basename', renders <MemoryRouter basename="/app" initialEntries={['/app/s/doc-1']}> around NavigationGuardProvider with an always-blocking guard and clicks a same-page link (to="/s/doc-1?tab=2"), asserting no prompt appears (line 149). It is non-vacuous: under a basename, useNavigate joins the basename before push so pathOf yields "/app/s/doc-1" (provider lines 40-42, createHref does not prepend basename), while useLocation yields the stripped "/s/doc-1"; without the basenamed() join at provider lines 49-51/115 the comparison would differ, leaving() would return true, the blocking guard would fire and PROMPT.title would render, failing line 149. The route /s/doc-1 does match under basename /app so Editor mounts and the guard is genuinely registered, and getByText('same document') would throw if the link were missing — so the test cannot pass for a degenerate reason. The reviewer's stated search ("grep 'basename' in packages/frontend/tests came up empty") is directly contradicted by lines 128/129/132/134 of that file.
